properties.description:
`get_skill` refusing an unknown name first says what the name IS, when it is one of the slash commands: "'rules' is the slash command; it is served as 'governance-proposal'". Six of the eight advertised commands map to a skill.

TWO OF THE EIGHT MAP TO NO SKILL AT ALL and the table says so rather than inventing one — `/decisions` calls `scan_nodes` for the Decision type and `/debt` calls `loop_status`. Answering those with a plausible skill name would send the caller somewhere that cannot help them, which is the failure the refusal exists to prevent.

SINCE 2026-09-24, A COMMAND THAT NAMES A SKILL IS SERVED, NOT REFUSED (chg:get-skill-serves-a-slash-command-2026-09-24).
- `get_skill("rules")`, "/rules", "gaps" and "/gaps" each return that skill, with `requested_as` saying what was asked for.
- The refusal described above now fires only for the commands that are TOOLS (/decisions, /debt, /next) and for names that are neither. It still names the tool to call.
- The refusal had been measured costing a chat model a round trip with only one possible answer (flo2, 2026-09-24).
properties.name: A refusal maps a user-facing command name to the skill actually served — or to the tool, when there is no skill
